research_question_candidate: Do published full TOFU checkpoints for Llama 3.2 3B and Llama 3.1 8B show materially different pre-unlearning answer-likelihood profiles on forget, retain, and holdout data?
interpretation_limit: The model pair differs in both parameter count and generation/training history; results are a checkpoint comparison, not a causal parameter-scaling effect.

dataset.retain_sample_rule: Include the two contiguous 20-QA profile blocks that contain both occurrences of the known conflicting question, then sample 18 other profile blocks without replacement from the remaining blocks using seed 42; use the same fixed blocks for both models.

baseline_diagnostic.official_metric: Per-example mean probability of the gold answer: exp(-mean assistant-token cross-entropy), matching Open-Unlearning's probability metric.

prompt.note: The pinned Open-Unlearning chat-template branch does not truncate to max_length; actual tokenized lengths are recorded by the runner.

baseline_diagnostic.uncertainty: Percentile 95% cluster-bootstrap interval over 20-QA profile blocks, 5,000 resamples, seed 42.
baseline_diagnostic.retention_collision_sensitivity: After preserving the official split for primary comparability, recompute retain statistics after excluding both instances of the identical question with conflicting answers.

official_metric_baseline.eight_b_outcome: Version 6 completed the isolated Llama 3.1 8B retain90 oracle evaluation in a fresh Kaggle runtime. It scored all 400 ordered forget10 rows in 423.93 seconds, passed the GPU-only T4x2 placement and generation smoke, and recorded the pinned checkpoint and evaluation data hashes. Kaggle and the independent local verifier both pass all four full/oracle checkpoints. For 8B, full and retain90-oracle forget-set Truth Ratio distributions are distinguishable (KS D=0.3900, p=1.5853e-27), consistent with the intended pre-unlearning baseline separation. This does not evaluate an unlearning method.
